title: LCROSS / CABEUS 2009 / REMOTE EVIDENCE STUDY
site: Permanently shadowed region within Cabeus crater, lunar south pole
coordinate_scope: Approximate crater context from NASA quick mission facts; not the LCROSS impact point. Coordinate reference frame is not specified by that summary. Do not use these values as a precise navigation target.
observed_water_context: Published maximum total water vapour plus water ice within the LCROSS instrument field of view. This is not the entire plume or a whole-crater inventory.
estimate_context: Site regolith mass fraction inferred using the estimated excavated regolith mass that reached sunlight and was observable. It is not a direct weighing of a sample returned by this player.
citation: Colaprete, A. et al. (2010). Detection of Water in the LCROSS Ejecta Plume. Science 330(6003), 463-468.

sources.supports: Original peer-reviewed analysis; water observation, maximum FOV quantity and site mass-fraction estimate with reported uncertainties.
LCROSS mission, south-polar Cabeus impact and water discovery context.
Appendix C approximate Cabeus crater context coordinates, 84.9 degrees S and 35.5 degrees W; not impact coordinates.
Public raw and calibrated mission archives. No raw spectrum from that archive is bundled or analysed by this exercise.

processing: Transcribe cited published numeric estimates and their units into a small factual JSON record.
Preserve reported plus/minus without assigning a confidence level that is not established here.
Compute 5.6 - 2.9 = 2.7 and 5.6 + 2.9 = 8.5 only as arithmetic endpoints of the reported expression, not guaranteed physical or statistical bounds.
Explain percent by mass using a hypothetical 100 kg comparison; do not label it a measured sample.
Keep this modern remote study separate from Apollo 12 location, historical cargo, terrain, oxygen and mission completion.
limitations: This product is a derived publication-facts summary, not raw spectral measurements or a new NASA result.
One impact site's inferred concentration does not establish water everywhere on the Moon, at Apollo 12, or at any point in the current game map.
The 100 kg comparison does not predict recoverable water or extraction yield.
No fabricated spectral points, drill measurements, player samples or local water detections are provided.
credit: Scientific facts: Colaprete et al. (2010), LCROSS science team; mission/archive context: NASA and NASA Planetary Data System. Derived exercise and arithmetic presentation: LunarRescue contributors with AI assistance.
rights: Facts transcribed and paraphrased with source attribution. No journal figure, abstract copy, PDF or licensed model is redistributed. NASA context remains subject to its media guidelines; no endorsement is implied.
